subject: Performance SLO / Context Window Follow-up (latency, concurrency, tokens)
messages:

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & context window (recap + next steps)

Hi Anita / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion, and appreciate you walking us through the FinCo production requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap from our call:
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile generation latency under 300ms for single-turn customer messages (avg token output ~80 tokens)
- Peak throughput target: 150 requests/sec with bursts to 300 RPS for short windows
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 40-60, occasionally spiking to ~120 during batch jobs
- Streaming requirement: client expects token-by-token streaming for chat UI (low-latency first token important)
- Context window: you indicated up to 12k input tokens (user history + metadata) with output up to 1k tokens in some workflows

Open questions we flagged during the call:
1) For the long context workflows, how often is the full 12k used vs. a trimmed/summarized context? (ballpark %)
2) Which endpoints must be streaming vs. can be non-streaming?
3) Are there hard throughput SLAs during business hours only or 24/7?

Attachments: SLO_worksheet.xlsx (strawman for latency/throughput test cases); redwood_perf_report.pdf (sample perf benchmarks)

Next steps we propose:
- You: confirm approximate % of requests that hit the full 12k context and which endpoints need streaming by Tue 2027-06-29
- Us: Rishi and the infra team will run targeted benchmarks (latency vs. context size, concurrency scaling, streaming startup latency) and share results and proposed config (batching, KV cache, quant profile) by Fri 2027-06-30
- Sync: 30m follow-up next week to review bench results and finalize mutual action plan

If that looks right I’ll compile the mutual action plan and schedule the bench runs.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & context window (recap + next steps)

Marissa — thanks for the concise recap. A few answers from our side: 

1) Context usage: roughly 70% of conversational traffic uses <= 4k tokens. About 20% uses 4k–8k, and ~10% hits 8k–12k (primarily support transcripts and compliance searches).
2) Streaming: our main chat UI (customer-facing) requires streaming. Backend batch analytics endpoints do not. First-token latency in the chat UI is critical — under 150ms preferred.
3) SLA window: business hours critical (US-East 8am–8pm) — outside that we accept degraded throughput but still want reasonable tail latency.

Also attaching a quick traffic breakdown CSV (see attached stub) and a doc describing our compliance-driven audit workflow that pushes long contexts.

Questions for your bench runs: can you show both cold-start (no KV cache) and warm-start (with prefix caching) numbers? Also please include streaming startup latency (time to first token) vs. total completion latency for 500-token outputs.

Carlos
Head of Product, FinCo
carlos.diaz@finco.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Diaz <carlos.diaz@finco.com>, Anita Sharma <anita@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & context window (recap + next steps)

Carlos / Anita — thanks, this is really helpful. Quick technical follow-up and what we’ll include in the bench: 

Bench plan (high level):
- Models: we’ll test a production-equivalent open model we’ve verified for throughput (quantized FP16 where applicable) and a slightly smaller variant for fallback scenarios.
- Context sizes: 2k, 4k, 8k, 12k inputs paired with outputs of 80, 300, and 500 tokens.
- Concurrency profiles: 20, 60, 120 concurrent sessions. We’ll run both steady-state and burst (4x) scenarios to simulate peak.
- Streaming metrics: time-to-first-token, median per-token emission delta, and end-to-end completion latency.
- Cache profiles: cold (no prefix cache), warm (prefix KV cached), and aggressive prefix-aggregation (where we compact history into a shorter summary to simulate your summarization option).

Important notes on expected behavior (so you have visibility into tradeoffs):
- Latency scales roughly linearly with total input + output tokens when running a single request end-to-end; large context lengths increase encoder/attention pass time and cache lookups add variability.
- For streaming, first-token latency is dominated by model warm-start and decoder init; pre-warming KV cache and keeping a hot pool reduces first-token latency substantially. We aim to demonstrate median time-to-first-token under 150ms in warm-warm scenarios for 80-token outputs; 500-token outputs will have higher completion latency but should still meet your SLO for first-token with proper pool sizing.
- Throughput at 150 RPS with 60 concurrency will require batching and adaptive kernel selection; we’ll show recommended batch sizes and the expected P95 latency for each config.

Deliverables by Fri:
- CSV of raw bench results (latency, throughput, tokens)
- Short recommendation doc: pool sizing, cache policy, streaming config, and a quantization/precision recommendation for cost/latency tradeoff
- Proposed mutual action plan with milestones for a pilot

If you can share a representative payload (anonymized chat transcript) for the 12k workflows that would help us simulate real token distributions.

Thanks — Rishi

Thanks team — this all sounds good.

Carlos / Anita: I’ve attached the mutual action plan (MAP) and populated the SLO worksheet with the bench scenarios Rishi outlined. Please review and either comment in the sheet or reply with edits by EOD Thurs so we can lock the pilot scope.

Quick note on asks we made during the call that are required to hit the first-token SLO for streaming:
- We’ll need a target 95th percentile CPU/GPU allocation window during business hours (approx % of reserved capacity you’re willing to commit) so we can size dedicated pools or recommend a Dedicated profile.
- If you have ops constraints that prevent pre-warming (e.g., strict cost controls), we’ll include a fallback plan using a smaller model for cold-starts and an automatic warm-up policy for expected bursts.

Next call: I’ll schedule a 30m slot for Mon 2027-07-04 to review bench outputs and finalize the MAP.
